title: The 10 Best Corded Hedge Trimmers
subtitle: Plug-in electric hedge trimmers and pole trimmers for shrubs and hedges, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A corded hedge trimmer runs as long as you like and costs less than a battery model with the same blade. We ranked 10 best-sellers from BLACK+DECKER, Sun Joe, SENIX and GARCARE on rating, review volume and features (a 22-inch or longer blade, 3/4-inch or bigger cut capacity, cord retention and a rotating handle or pivoting head). Three are pole trimmers for tall hedges. All of them need an outdoor extension cord, sold separately. For battery trimmers, see our cordless hedge trimmer page.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: Grasstigon 24" Electric Hedge Trimmer Corded 5A with 180 Degree Rotating Handle
avoid.flag: Listing contradicts itself on motor size and cut width
avoid.verdict: The listing can't agree on its own motor: the title and bullets say 5 A, the part number says 4.5 A, and the spec table gives a 6.38-inch cutting width for a 24-inch blade.
reasons: The title and bullets advertise a 5A motor, but the manufacturer part number is Gt-24c-4.5a.
The spec table lists a cutting width of 6.38 inches for a 24 in blade.
It never states the thickest branch it can cut, only a 0.94 in blade gap. The BLACK+DECKER BEHT350FF states 3/4 in for $59.

buyers_guide.a: Corded trimmers cost less, never need charging and are usually lighter than a battery model with the same blade. You give up range: you have to stay within an extension cord's reach of an outlet. For hedges along the house or a small yard, corded is the cheaper choice.

buyers_guide.q: What blade length do I need?
buyers_guide.a: 16 to 18 inches is enough for shrubs and foundation plantings. For hedges longer than about 10 feet, a 22 to 24 inch blade covers more in each pass. Longer blades weigh more, which you notice when trimming above shoulder height.

It's the thickest branch the blade gap will take, usually 5/8 to 3/4 inch on corded trimmers. Anything thicker needs loppers or a pruning saw. The BLACK+DECKER BEHTS300 adds a saw tip rated for branches up to 1.5 inches.

buyers_guide.q: Do I need a pole hedge trimmer?
buyers_guide.a: Only if your hedges are taller than you can reach comfortably from the ground, roughly 6 feet. Pole models weigh 7.5 to 8.9 lb here, against about 3.9 to 7 lb for the handhelds, and the weight sits at the far end of the pole.

buyers_guide.q: What extension cord should I use?
buyers_guide.a: An outdoor-rated cord. For a 3 to 5 amp trimmer, a 16-gauge cord is fine up to 100 feet. Most trimmers here have a cord retainer; loop the cord through it so it doesn't pull out of the trimmer mid-cut, and keep the cord behind you, away from the blade.
